title: The fixed square is Cartesian
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient
conventions, $A=A_{E,n}$, put $s=\Spec k$, and let
$c=(c_1,c_2):C\to X\times_sX$ be a
cohomological correspondence with
fixed scheme
$F=\operatorname{Fix}(c)$ of [def-trf-fixed-scheme] and projections
$i_F:F\to C$, $d:F\to X$. Then the square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
F & \xrightarrow{i_F} & C\\
{\scriptstyle d}\downarrow & & \downarrow{\scriptstyle c}\\
X & \xrightarrow{\Delta_X} & X\times_sX
\end{array}
$$

is Cartesian, the composites
$c_1i_F$ and $c_2i_F$ both equal $d$, and the identity
$\Delta_Xd=ci_F$ holds. Moreover the composition law for the
exceptional inverse image gives

$$
Rd^!\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Ri_F^!Rc_1^!
$$

as a natural isomorphism of functors $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)\to D^b_{ctf}(F,A)$
(the adjoint form of the composition law $R(c_1i_F)_!\cong Rc_{1!}Ri_{F!}$ of [thm-sf-comp-composition],
as $d=c_1i_F$). The displayed isomorphism is a composition comparison for $d=c_1i_F$.

proof.text: By [def-trf-fixed-scheme], $F=C\times_{X\times_sX,c,\Delta_X}X$ with its specified projections $i_F,d$. In particular $ci_F=\Delta_Xd$. Explicitly, for every scheme $T$ and morphisms $a:T\to C$, $b:T\to X$ satisfying $ca=\Delta_Xb$, the defining universal property gives a unique $t:T\to F$ with $i_Ft=a$ and $dt=b$. This is exactly the Cartesian-square condition of [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], with the canonical identification of $F$ with the displayed fibre product.

Let $p_1,p_2:X\times_sX\to X$ be the two product projections. By definition of $c=(c_1,c_2)$ and of the diagonal, $p_jc=c_j$ and $p_j\Delta_X=\mathrm{id}_X$. Applying $p_j$ to $ci_F=\Delta_Xd$ gives $c_ji_F=d$ for $j=1,2$. These agree with the projection identities recorded in [def-trf-fixed-scheme]. Thus the commutativity identity and both leg identities hold as identities of scheme morphisms, not merely on points.

Check the geometric hypotheses for the functors. By [def-trf-correspondence], $X$ and $C$ are separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Since separatedness means the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-proper-morphism], $\Delta_X$ is closed. The Cartesian square of Step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b),(c) make $i_F$ a closed immersion and hence proper, separated and finite type. Its affine inverse images have coordinate rings $B/I$ for affine charts $\operatorname{Spec}B\subset C$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]; a finite affine $k$-cover of $C$ therefore gives a finite affine cover of $F$ by finitely generated $k$-algebras, so $F$ is finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Separatedness of $F/k$ follows by composition from [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e). Apply [lemma-nagata-finite-type-to-separated-target] to the triangles $C\to X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $F\to X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$: $c_1$ and $d$ are finite type. They are separated as well: for either $T=C,F$ and $h:T\to X$, the square expressing $\Delta_{T/X}$ as the pullback of $\Delta_{T/k}$ along $T\times_XT\to T\times_kT$ is Cartesian by the fibre-product universal property; [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b) makes this diagonal closed. Thus $i_F,c_1,d$ are all separated finite-type morphisms between separated finite-type $k$-schemes.

The targets $C,X$ of these three morphisms are quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine], applied to their separated finite-type structure maps to the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Thus [thm-nagata-compactification] supplies a compactification $T\xrightarrow{j}\overline T\xrightarrow{p}Y$ for each of $i_F,c_1,d$. The proper map $p$ is finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism]. To check that $\overline T$ is finite type over $k$, cover $Y$ by finitely many affine finite-type $k$-charts and each inverse image by finitely many affine finite-type charts over that chart. Composing the two finite lists of algebra generators gives finitely generated $k$-algebras and a finite affine cover, precisely [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Each $\overline T$ therefore has finite dimension by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]; choose a nonnegative integral upper bound (choose $0$ for the empty scheme). These are exactly the compactification and dimension hypotheses needed for the bounded-class adjunction in the next steps.

Use ordinary constant-$A_{E,n}$ module coefficients and the constructible exceptional functor of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], rather than an unrestricted ambient pro-etale right adjoint. Every object of $D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$, being bounded constructible, has a bounded etale-origin witness by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii). By [thm-sf-preservation-class](1),(2) for the three maps of Step 3, $Rd^!N$ and $Ri_F^!Rc_1^!N$ lie in $D^b_{ctf}(F,A)$ whenever $N\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$; the intermediate $Rc_1^!N$ is bounded below. All targets here are separated finite-type $k$-schemes, as required by that theorem. The coefficient ring is exactly the finite ring $A=A_{E,n}$ with $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$ fixed in [def-trf-coefficient-conventions].

For $M\in D^b_{ctf}(F,A)$ and $N\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, apply [thm-sf-comp-composition] with $f=i_F$, $g=c_1$ and $g f=d$ from Step 2. It gives $\alpha:Rc_{1!}Ri_{F!}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rd_!$ on bounded-below etale-origin inputs, and says that the compact-support functors preserve that class. Thus $Ri_{F!}M$ is a valid source input to the bounded-class adjunction for $c_1$. The natural Hom bijections of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class](2), with the exceptional functors of Step 5, give
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_F(M,Rd^!N)&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(Rd_!M,N)\\
&\xrightarrow{\alpha_M^*}\operatorname{Hom}_X(Rc_{1!}Ri_{F!}M,N)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_C(Ri_{F!}M,Rc_1^!N)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_F(M,Ri_F^!Rc_1^!N).
\end{aligned}$$
The outer source inputs have etale origin by Step 5; the middle one has etale origin and is bounded below by the composition theorem. The target inputs $N,Rc_1^!N$ are bounded below by Step 5. Compactifications with finite dimension bounds were fixed in Step 4. Hence every application has precisely the domain its cited statement allows. The second arrow is precomposition by $\alpha_M$, so the resulting comparison has the requested direction $Rd^!\to Ri_F^!Rc_1^!$.

Write $P=Rd^!N$ and $Q=Ri_F^!Rc_1^!N$, both in $D^b_{ctf}(F,A)$ by Step 5, and denote Step 6's natural bijection by $H_M:\operatorname{Hom}(M,P)\to\operatorname{Hom}(M,Q)$. Put $a=H_P(\mathrm{id}_P):P\to Q$ and $b=H_Q^{-1}(\mathrm{id}_Q):Q\to P$. Naturality in $M$ gives $H_M(v)=a v$; thus $ab=\mathrm{id}_Q$, while $H_P(ba)=aba=a=H_P(\mathrm{id}_P)$ and injectivity gives $ba=\mathrm{id}_P$. Consequently $a$ is an isomorphism. For a morphism $u:N\to N'$, put $P(u)=Rd^!(u)$ and $Q(u)=Ri_F^!Rc_1^!(u)$, and write $H^N,H^{N'}$ for the two Hom bijections. Naturality in the target variable gives $Q(u)a_N=H^{N'}_{P_N}(P(u))$. Naturality in the source variable, applied to $P(u):P_N\to P_{N'}$, gives $H^{N'}_{P_N}(P(u))=a_{N'}P(u)$. Thus $Q(u)a_N=a_{N'}P(u)$, so these components form the asserted natural isomorphism $Rd^!\xrightarrow{\sim}Ri_F^!Rc_1^!$ on $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$. Its construction from precomposition by $\alpha$ is exactly the adjoint composition comparison.

split_report.summary: Expanded the fixed-product definition into its universal property and both scheme-morphism identities. Checked finite-type/separatedness, compactifications, finite dimension, etale-origin inputs and constructible finite-Tor preservation before spelling out the Hom-bijection proof and its inverse maps. Reused existing nodes throughout, with no new nodes or Lean attachment. STATEMENT-DISPUTED: the source’s informal exclusivity word "only" is literally false since d=c_2 i_F also gives the exceptional composition comparison; retained every displayed claim and replaced the exclusivity wording by the nonexclusive composition interpretation. Second reading by N7 made the intended finite-Tor constructible functor domain explicit and expanded naturality in the target object into its two Hom-bijection equations; no proof route, hypotheses, or displayed conclusion changed.
